Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation and appreciate the clarity on your use cases. Quick recap and a couple asks so we can map the next steps: 

Summary: 
- Primary use case: low-latency customer-facing summarization and routing (peak concurrent users ~120).
- Key decision criteria called out on the call: latency targets, per-token cost, deployment model (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and SLAs/compliance.

Asks/next steps: 
1) Can you confirm the economic buyer and the security/legal/procurement contacts we should loop in? If you can share names/emails and the procurement timeline that'd be ideal.
2) For latency: you mentioned a 200ms p95 token latency target for interactive flows — can you confirm if that applies to all endpoints or just the critical routing flow?
3) We can share a draft SLA and a short deployment options note — would you prefer DocuSign for formal review or Slack/email?

I'll follow up later this week with a short note that summarizes how Redwood would meet the latency/cost tradeoffs and an initial SLA draft. Attaching the security questionnaire you mentioned (placeholder) for us to review before Rishi's team starts compiling evidence.

Attachments: Finova_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (placeholder)

Thanks,

Thanks Sophie — super helpful. Two quick clarifying questions before we prepare the SLA and deployment notes: 

1) For the 200ms p95 routing target, is that measured end-to-end (client -> our API -> model -> back to client) or from the API boundary (i.e., excluding client-side network)? We typically benchmark p95 latency at the API boundary but can provide guidance for end-to-end expectations.

2) On deployment mode: can you indicate which of these is most likely for Finova in production? (select one if you can): hosted (Redwood API), dedicated reserved capacity, or private (VPC/on-prem). If you’re unsure, is the primary constraint security/compliance or predictable latency/cost?

We're preparing an SLA draft (will attach v1) and a short comparison doc outlining latency/cost tradeoffs across deployment modes. Will send by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Sophie — looping in a short technical note and attaching the SLA draft (SLA_Draft_v2.docx). Below are concise answers to Marissa's questions: 

- Latency measurement: our standard is API boundary p95 (model response + runtime overhead). For typical hosted configurations we can expect ~120-180ms p95 for short-form completion flows; routing classifiers at small context sizes are commonly ~80-150ms p95 depending on model and batching. End-to-end client-to-client will add network variance — we can run a simple client-side measurement test if you want.

- Deployment guidance: given you cited security/procurement involvement, common pattern we see is starting on Redwood Hosted for evaluation and early production, then moving to Dedicated Reserved Capacity or Private for regulated workloads that require strict network controls or on-prem data residency. Dedicated typically gives the best balance of predictable latency and cost.

- SLA highlights: 99.9% uptime target for Dedicated; response latency SLOs can be contractually defined per-route with escalation playbooks. See attached for full language.

Attachments: SLA_Draft_v2.docx (redwood draft; editable)

If you want, Rishi and I can join a 30-min call with Heather and Mark to walk through evidence for the security questionnaire and the SLA. Proposed slots: July 15/16.

Thanks,
Laura
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
